text: Before fear could silence the smaller creatures, the Pied Kingfisher fluttered onto a reed right before the eagle’s eyes.
'Great King of the sky,' the little bird chirped fearlessly.
'If your talons drive us away from the shallows, who will watch the river reeds to warn you when the crocodile rises?
Who will disturb the weed beds so the large fish swim up into your view?
A river where only the strong eat will soon become a river where the strong starve alone.'
The truth struck like an arrow.
The Eagle bowed his white-crowned head.
The birds divided the pools by hours—some by dawn, some by dusk—and the river sustained every wing until the rains returned.
